<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>Æ</c>térnæ Regi glóriæ
Devóta laudum cántica
Fidéles solvant hódie
Pro Coróna Domínica.

<h>C</h>orónat Regem ómnium
Coróna contuméliæ,
Cuius nobis oppróbrium
Corónam confert glóriæ.

<h>D</h>e spinárum acúleis
Christi Coróna pléctitur,
Qua minístris tartáreis
Mundi potéstas tóllitur.

<h>C</h>oróna Christi cápitis
Sacro perfúsa sánguine,
Pœnis solátis débitis,
Reos purgat a crímine.

<h>L</h>aus Christo, Regi glóriæ,
Pro Corónæ virtútibus,
Qua nos refórmans grátiæ
Corónet in cæléstibus.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Hebrǽos
<r>Cap. 2</r>
<c>N</c>on ángelis subiécit Deus orbem terræ futúrum de quo lóquimur. Testátus est autem in quodam loco quis dicens: Quid est homo, quod memor es eius, aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum ? Minuísti eum paulo minus ab ángelis; glória et honóre coronásti eum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum: ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius. In eo enim quod ómnia ei subiécit, nihil dimísit non subiéctum ei; nunc autem necdum vidémus ómnia subiécta ei. Eum autem, qui módico quam ángeli minorátus est, vidémus Iesum propter passiónem mortis glória et honóre coronátum, ut grátia Dei pro ómnibus gustáret mortem.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Spina carens Flos spina púngitur, per quam culpæ spina confríngitur:
* Spina mortis spinis retúnditur, dum Vita móritur, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Per hoc ludíbrium hostis delúditur: mortis domínium per mortem tóllitur.
<r>℟.</r> Spina mortis spinis retúnditur, dum Vita móritur, allelúia.

<r>Benedictio.</r> Quorum festum cólimus, ipsi intercédant pro nobis ad Dóminum.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>D</c>écebat enim eum, propter quem ómnia et per quem ómnia, qui multos fílios in glóriam addúxerat, auctórem salútis eórum per passiónem consummáre. Qui enim sanctíficat et qui sanctificántur, ex uno omnes; propter quam causam non confúnditur fratres eos vocáre, dicens: Nuntiábo nomen tuum frátribus meis, in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te; et íterum: Ego ero fidens in eum; et íterum: Ecce ego et púeri mei, quos dedit mihi Deus. Quia ergo púeri communicavérunt carni et sánguini, et ipse simíliter participávit eísdem, ut per mortem destrúeret eum qui habébat mortis impérium, id est diábolum; et liberáret eos qui timóre mortis per totam vitam obnóxii erant servitúti.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Corónat Regem ómnium Iudǽa Serto spíneo: stat inter spinas lílium vernans cruóre róseo,
* Spinárum culpæ néscium, spinæ punctum acúleo, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Sub decóre fulget purpúreo corpus nitens candóre níveo.
<r>℟.</r> Spinárum culpæ néscium, spinæ punctum acúleo, allelúia.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>C</c>um sanctus Ludovícus, rex Francórum, a Balduíno secúndo, Constantinopolitáno imperatóre, Corónam Dómini spíneam dono accepísset, duos ex órdine Prædicatórum fratres, Andréam et Iacóbum, Constantinópolim misit. Qui in crástino sancti Lauréntii Mártyris, anno millésimo ducentésimo trigésimo nono, Corónam regi Sénone detulérunt. Quæ, magna cum solemnitáte Parísios deláta, postrémo apud régium palátium collocáta est, in capélla ab ipso Ludovíco ædificáta. Thesáurus iste pretiósus, lugéndis tumúltus gállici tempóribus sǽculo décimo octávo exeúnte ímpie subréptus ac póstmodum restitútus, in metropolitánam basílicam translátus est. Quasdam vero Corónæ sacræ spinas rex Ludovícus Frátribus Prædicatóribus dono dedit, illísque susceptiónis anniversárium in capélla Corónæ dicáta celebrándum commísit. Festum Sanctíssimæ Corónæ, circa medietátem sǽculi décimi tértii, kalendário órdinis Prædicatórum insértum est.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Felix Spina, cuius acúlei guttis rubent roris sanguínei,
* Vires frangunt regis tartárei, seras pandunt regni sidérei, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> O Spinárum imménsa glória, quæ tot nobis præstant remédia.
<r>℟.</r> Vires frangunt regis tartárei, seras pandunt regni sidérei, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Allelúia.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>W</c>e praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.
To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.
To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.
<n>bow head</n> Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;
Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.
The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.
The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.
The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.
The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;
The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.
Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;
Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.
Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.
Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.
<n>During the following verse all make a profound bow:</n> When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.
When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.
We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.
<n>Kneel for the following verse</n> We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.
O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.
Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.
Day by day * we magnify thee;
<n>During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow.</n> And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.
O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.
O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.
O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>éptimo Kaléndas Maii Luna undevicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ Litaníæ maióres ad sanctum Petrum.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ natális beáti Marci Evangelístæ. Hic, discípulus et intérpres Apóstoli Petri, rogátus Romæ a frátribus scripsit Evangélium, quo assúmpto, perréxit in Ægýptum, primúsque Alexandríæ Christum annúntians, constítuit Ecclésiam; ac póstea, pro fide Christi tentus, fúnibus vinctus et per saxa raptátus, gráviter afflíctus est; deínde, reclúsus in cárcere, primo angélica visitatióne confortátus est, et demum, ipso Dómino sibi apparénte, ad cæléstia regna vocátus, octávo Nerónis anno.
<h>I</h>tem Alexandríæ sancti Aniáni Epíscopi, qui, beáti Marci discípulus eiúsque in Episcopátu succéssor, clarus virtútibus quiévit in Dómino.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ sancti Stéphani, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui ab hæréticis Synódum Chalcedonénsem impugnántibus, multa passus, in Oróntem flúvium præcipitátus est, témpore Zenónis Imperatóris.
<h>S</h>yracúsis, in Sicília, sanctórum Mártyrum fratrum Evódii, Hermógenis et Callístæ.
<h>L</h>áubiis, in Bélgio, natális sancti Ermíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ sanctórum Philónis et Agathopódis Diaconórum, de quibus beátus Ignátius, Epíscopus et Martyr, laudábilem in suis epístolis mentiónem facit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.479546a6cd:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 25th 2027, the 19th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

<h>A</h>t Rome, the Greater Litanies, [instituted in sixth century by Pope St. Gregory I, The Great,] take place at St Peter's Church.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the blessed Evangelist Mark. He was the disciple and interpreter of the Apostle Peter. He wrote his Gospel at the prayer of the brethren at Rome. He took it with him and went to Egypt, where he was the first man who proclaimed Christ at Alexandria, and where he founded that Church. He was afterward arrested as a believer in Christ, bound with cords, and dragged over stones to his grievous suffering. Then he was remanded to prison, where he was comforted first by a visitation of angels and then by the Lord Himself appearing unto him, and was called unto the kingdom of heaven in the 8th year of Nero, [in the year 68.]
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, holy Anian, Pope of that see. He was the disciple of blessed Mark, and held that Papacy.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, [in the year 479] the holy martyr Stephen, Patriarch of that see, who suffered many things at the hands of the heretics who assailed the Council of Chalcedon, and was cast into the river Orontes, in the time of the Emperor Zeno.
<h>A</h>t Syracuse, the holy martyrs Evodius, Hermogenes, and Kallistas. [They were brothers and sister.]
<h>A</h>t Antioch, [in the second century,] the holy Deacons Philo and Agathopodes, of whom the blessed Ignatius, Bishop and martyr, maketh honourable mention in his epistles.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Rom 6:9-10</r>
<c>C</c>hristus resúrgens ex mórtuis iam non móritur, mors illi ultra non dominábitur. Quod enim mórtuus est peccáto, mórtuus est semel: quod autem vivit, vivit Deo.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Si oblítus fúero tui, allelúia, obliviscátur mei déxtera mea, allelúia.
* Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Super flúmina Babylónis illic sédimus et flévimus, dum recordarémur tui, Sion, allelúia.
<r>℟.</r> Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>A</c>d cenam Agni próvidi,
Et stolis albis cándidi,
Post tránsitum maris Rubri,
Christo canámus Príncipi.

<h>C</h>uius corpus sanctíssimum,
In ara crucis tórridum,
Cruóre eius róseo
Gustándo vívimus Deo.

<h>P</h>rotécti Paschæ véspere
A devastánte Angelo,
Erépti de duríssimo
Pharaónis império.

<h>I</h>am Pascha nostrum Christus est,
Qui immolátus agnus est:
Sinceritátis ázyma,
Caro eius obláta est.

<h>O</h> vere digna hóstia,
Per quam fracta sunt tártara,
Redémpta plebs captiváta,
Réddita vitæ prǽmia.

<h>C</h>onsúrgit Christus túmulo,
Victor redit de bárathro,
Tyránnum trudens vínculo,
Et Paradísum réserans.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc pascháli gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Mane nobíscum, Dómine, allelúia.
<r>℟.</r> Quóniam advesperáscit, allelúia.
b.987a47c936:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Rom 6:9-10</r>
<c>K</c>nowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him. For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> If I forget thee, Alleluia, let my right hand forget me, alleluia.
* If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> By the rivers of Babylon there we sat down and wept, when we remembered thee, O Zion, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>A</c>t the Lamb’s high feast we sing
Praise to our victorious King,
Who hath washed us in the tide
Flowing from his piercèd side.

<h>P</h>raise we him whose love divine
Gives the guests his blood for wine,
Gives his body for the feast,
Love the victim, love the priest.

<h>W</h>here the paschal blood is poured,
Death’s dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel’s hosts triumphant go
Through the wave that drowns the foe.

<h>C</h>hrist, the Lamb whose blood was shed,
Paschal victim, paschal bread;
With sincerity and love
Eat we manna from above.

<h>M</h>ighty victim from the sky,
Powers of hell beneath thee lie;
Death is conquered in the fight;
Thou hast brought us life and light.

<h>N</h>ow thy banner thou dost wave;
Vanquished Satan and the grave;
Angels join his praise to tell —
See o’erthrown the prince of hell.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
